title: Strategy Week synthesis and exec brief
summary: Working synthesis from Strategy Week (Feb 2026). Combines draft company OKRs for H2 2026, executive talking points for the March all-hands, and a short cross-functional alignment checklist. This is a slimmed working brief intended for exec review and for the all-hands prep thread. Not final — many KRs still need owner commitments and metric baselines.
objective_summaries:
O1: Make inference predictable and cheaper for customers — focus on RU/unit economics, batching, and quantization tooling.
O2: Expand enterprise readiness — Private deployments + Dedicated SLAs + compliance checklist.
O3: Developer growth and platform adoption — improve onboarding funnel, SDK parity, and reference apps.
O4: Operational reliability — 99.95% platform availability for paid tiers and improved SLO visibility in Console.
okrs_draft:
OKR 1 — Lower inference unit cost while maintaining QPS/latency SLOs:
- KR1.1: Reduce per-token compute cost by 25% on top 5 models by usage (baseline Jan 2026).
- KR1.2: Ship automatic prefix caching for hosted API and show 15% cost savings on synthetic RL workload.
- KR1.3: Add two quantization profiles (4-bit float eq.) and report perf/cost tradeoffs in Optimize dashboard.

OKR 2 — Enterprise: make Private/Dedicated the obvious choice for regulated customers:
- KR2.1: Close 3 pilot Private deployments (legal/infra approved) with average time-to-prod < 8 weeks.
- KR2.2: Deliver KMS + audit-log integrations and pass an internal compliance checklist for SOC pre-audit.
- KR2.3: Launch Dedicated offering with 99.9% SLA and published latency SLOs on product site.

OKR 3 — Developer velocity and adoption:
- KR3.1: Increase active API integrations (monthly active keys) by 40% vs baseline.
- KR3.2: Reduce median time-to-first-inference via quickstart templates to <10 minutes.
- KR3.3: Publish 4 reference apps including embeddings + retrieval example in repos and docs.

OKR 4 — Reliability and observability:
- KR4.1: Implement token-level trace sampling in Console and enable root-cause dashboards for 90% of incidents.
- KR4.2: Reduce tail latency P99 by 20% on hosted API through routing/backpressure improvements.
- KR4.3: Create automated canary rollouts and rollback policy across model catalog.
measurable_assumptions:
- Baselines: Jan 2026 telemetry will be used for cost/usage baselines; infra team to confirm export by Mar 1.
- Customer impact: cost reduction innovations must not increase P99 latency beyond current SLOs.
- Engineering resourcing: assume +6 FTEs in serving/runtime and +2 in product for H2 projects — hiring risk noted.
- Sales cycle: Dedicated/Private pilots require Sales + Solutions engineering support; lead time often 10–12 weeks unless pre-approved templates used.
allhands_agenda:
(30m) Exec topline — where we are and company priorities (Claire)
(20m) Roadmap highlights — hosted API, Dedicated availability, Private pilots (Miguel)
(15m) Ops + Reliability update — incidents, actions, SLOs (SRE lead)
(20m) Product deep dive — Optimize recommendations and customer stories (Product)
(10m) Culture & people — hiring highlights and Q2 people plan (People Ops)
(15m) Live Q&A — pre-collected + live questions; execs rotate answers
Note: reserve last 10 minutes for cross-team asks and commitments (slido + follow-up doc)
exec_update_notes:
Topline metrics to call out in all-hands: net revenue retention stable at 112% (FY run-rate), hosted API token growth +18% QoQ, Dedicated signed pilot commitments up 2x vs last quarter.
Risks to flag: hiring delays in serving-runtime, increased GPU spot market volatility affecting burst capacity costs, compliance checklist still incomplete for two targeted regions.
Three stories to lead with: 1) customer case where Dedicated cut latency variance by half; 2) Optimize pilot that reduced per-request cost by 12% for a mid-market SaaS; 3) internal SLO improvements that reduced incident recovery time.
Prep: ask each exec to have 2 slides (current metric, one tangible ask) and 3 anticipated Qs + brief answers in the shared folder.
